records.rationale: Retain November for seasonal garden foliage based on independently extracted JNTO autumn and Tokyo pages. GO TOKYO was not retrievable, so remove unsupported reliance on its ginkgo/windy-day/mountain details; describe broad autumn-garden appeal without promising a peak date.
records.why: November brings autumn-garden appeal, with Tokyo’s maples adding seasonal color as the weather cools.
records.tradeoff: Cooler evenings call for layers; leaf color varies with the year and location, so check garden conditions rather than assuming peak foliage on your dates.

records.rationale: Replace with existing eligible Seville. Maldives Meteorological Service explicitly places November in the normal southwest wet monsoon; year-round warmth and sunny gaps do not establish a November-specific Goldilocks advantage. Seville is present in destinationGuides and BEST_MONTHS includes November. Direct AEMET November normals establish substantially lower heat than Seville summer, while the replacement candidly discloses rain and cool nights. This is an evidence-based editorial substitution, not a computed global top-six ranking.
records.why: November’s milder days make Seville’s streets and monuments easier to explore than during its intense summer heat.
records.tradeoff: Rain is part of November, and nights are cool. Pack layers and a wet-weather option; this is a mild-weather choice, not a dry-season guarantee.

records.rationale: Official tourism page directly covers November–December long, warm, largely dry days as peak season begins and summer wind rises. The existing trade-off already prevents mislabelling it a quiet shoulder-season bargain.
records.why: Longer, warmer days usher in the outdoor season, with generally less rain than winter.
records.tradeoff: Peak season is beginning rather than absent, and summer winds are picking up.

records.rationale: Preserve the December lead: official weather page supports longest daylight and summer beach appeal. Add a sourced high-season caveat: Tourism Australia explicitly labels November–February high season, and Destination NSW warns of Bondi summer crowds. Peak season can be valid when visible, but December is not a crowd/value sweet spot.
records.why: December brings Sydney's longest daylight hours as summer warmth opens up beach days.
records.tradeoff: December is high season and popular beaches can be crowded. Summer humidity, rain and strong sun remain part of the trade-off.

records.rationale: Unlike wet-monsoon November, MMS identifies December as a transition toward the northeast monsoon. Existing wording already says transition, not established dry season. Retain conditionally for warm island travel, with no dependable-dry or shoulder-value promise.
records.why: Tropical warmth offers a winter escape while December transitions toward the northeast monsoon.
records.tradeoff: December is a transition month; the meteorological dry season is January–March, and showers remain possible.

records.rationale: Official November–December guidance supports warm, long outdoor days, rising wind and peak crowds. Existing trade-off is appropriately prominent; high-season weather appeal can justify inclusion without inventing value or quietness.
records.why: Long, balmy days bring beach time and the city's lively outdoor summer atmosphere.
records.tradeoff: This is peak-season territory, not a quiet escape; attractions draw crowds and winds can be strong.

records.rationale: The official city guide distinguishes winter from summer heavy rain and explicitly warns that December–February nights/early mornings can approach freezing. Existing copy covers the thermal edge and strong sun; retain as daytime city travel, not a reliably warm evening escape.
records.why: The less-rainy winter period makes a useful backdrop for daytime city exploring.
records.tradeoff: Nights and early mornings can be close to freezing; winter sunshine is not necessarily gentle.

records.rationale: Historical WMO/Thai Meteorological Department normals confirm a much drier, comparatively cooler December while daytime highs remain hot. Existing note correctly says relative cooling rather than cool climate. Use the old baseline for seasonality only, not a current forecast.
records.why: December combines one of the city's drier periods with relatively cooler seasonal temperatures.
records.tradeoff: Relatively cooler is still hot by day, and low average rainfall is not a promise of dry days.

records.rationale: Retain conditionally rather than force replacement: official city guidance identifies December as spring until late month and then summer, supporting warm-season exploration. Strengthen the caveat because spring rainfall explicitly extends through December and summer brings humid midday heat. Do not describe all December as mild spring or a dry sweet spot.
records.why: Late spring gives way to summer, with warmer days for visitors seeking a Southern Hemisphere escape.
records.tradeoff: Spring rain extends into December; late-month summer brings humid heat, especially at midday. This is not a reliably mild, dry sweet spot.
